Reference Label Generation Rules for the Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics

Overview

This document specifies a set of Label Generation Rules (LGR) for Inuktitut and Algonquian languages in Canada using a Syllabic Script known as CANS or UCAS (Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics) for the second level domain. The format of this file follows [RFC 7940].

This LGR is designed to be used in a zone that does cater to French IDNs. This LGR includes features that support its use in context of a French LGR in the same zone.

For details and additional background on the Canadian Aboriginal script, see “Proposal for Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics (UCAS) Script Reference LGR” [Proposal-Canadian Aboriginal].

Repertoire

The repertoire for the Unified Canadian Unified Syllabics Script contains 293 syllabics characters in contemporary use for Inuktitut and 12 other languages, including associated marks as defined in Section 5.1, “Included Code Points” in [Proposal-Canadian Aboriginal].

Principal Languages Covered

The UCAS script is a script primarily used by First Nations and Inuit in Canada. It is a unique writing system structured around representing syllables.

In addition to Inuktitut, the following Algonquian languages using syllabic script are supported in the repertoire:

  • Naskapi, Northern Eastern Cree and Southern Eastern Cree used in the Eastern part of Canada.
  • Moose Cree, Eastern Swampy Cree, Western Swampy Cree, Woods Cree, Plains Cree, Oji-Cree, Ojibway, and Saulteaux used in the Western part of Canada.

For the second level, the repertoire has been augmented with the ASCII digits, U+0030 to U+0039, plus U+002D HYPHEN-MINUS, for a total of 304 repertoire elements.

Any code points outside the Canadian Aboriginal Script repertoire that are targets for out-of-repertoire variants would be included here only if the variant is listed in this file. In this case they are identified as a reflexive (identity) variant of type “out-of-repertoire-var”. Whether or not they are listed, they do not form part of the repertoire.

Repertoire Listing: Each code point or range is tagged with the script or scripts with which the code point is used and one or more other character categories. For each repertoire element, one or more references document sufficient justification for inclusion in the repertoire; see the “References” below. For code points in the repertoire, comments identify the language using the code point.

Variants

A number of in-script variants have been defined, in some cases based on regional alternation of the same letter.

A number of letters bear strong similarity to Latin letters, these have been given cross-script variant mappings.

Digit Variants: The Canadian Aboriginal reference LGR does not include native digits, so there are no semantic variants defined.

The specification of variants in this LGR follows the guidelines in [RFC 8228].

This LGR does not define allocatable variants.

Character Classes

The LGR defines the following character classes.

  • final-marks — final marks. Note that U+1505 CANADIAN SYLLABICS S is not considered a final mark based on its usage in Naskapi.
  • Common-digits — the set of ASCII digits.

Whole Label Evaluation (WLE) and Context Rules

Common Rules

By default, the LGR includes the rules and actions to implement the following restrictions mandated by the IDNA protocol. They are marked with ⍟.

  • Hyphen Restrictions — restrictions on the allowable placement of hyphens (no leading/ending hyphen and no hyphen in positions 3 and 4). These restrictions are described in Section 4.2.3.1 of RFC 5891 [5891]. They are implemented here as a context rule on U+002D (-) HYPHEN-MINUS.
  • Leading Combining Marks — restrictions on the allowable placement of combining marks (no leading combining mark). This rule is described in Section 4.2.3.2 of RFC 5891 [5891].

Script-specific rules in this LGR already prevent combining marks in leading position, making the “leading-combining-mark” rule technically redundant. It is retained here for consistency.

Default Actions

This LGR includes the complete set of default actions for LGRs, as well as the action needed to invalidate labels with misplaced combining marks. They are marked with ⍟. For a description see [RFC 7940] and [5891]. An additional action is triggered by mixed digit labels.

Script-specific Rules

The LGR defines the following script-specific rules concerning the placement of final marks and preventing some combinations.

  • leading-final-mark — A context rule on final mark characters that prohibits labels with a final mark at the start of the label or following a hyphen or digit. Final marks may not follow another final mark: only clusters composed into a single character, like U+1585, are allowed.
  • following-1550 — A context rule that prohibits the character following U+1550 CANADIAN SYLLABICS R.
  • following-1595 — A context rule that prohibits the character following U+1595 CANADIAN SYLLABICS NG.
  • following-1595-or-1596 — A context rule that prohibits the character from following U+1595 CANADIAN SYLLABICS NG or U+1596 CANADIAN SYLLABICS NNG.
  • followed-by-1483-1484-1553-or-155E — Restriction for code point U+1427 CANADIAN SYLLABICS FINAL MIDDLE DOT
  • restrictions-for-1505 — Restrictions for code point U+1505 CANADIAN SYLLABICS S. The character can be at any position in the label, but can only follow a character that is not a final mark or the following subset of final marks: U+1449, U+1466, U+1483, U+14D0, or U+153E. It can only be followed by the end of the label or the following subset of final marks U+1466, U+1483, U+1484 or U+14A1. It cannot be repeated. The treatment of U+1505 covers usage of this character in the Naskapi language.

Methodology

This Second Level Reference LGR for the Canadian Aboriginal Script was developed based on the proposal from the Unified Canadian Aboriginal Syllabics Script Reference LGR Generation Panel (UCAS WG) and edited by Asmus Freytag based on community feedback and public review. See [Proposal-Canadian Aboriginal] for methodology and contributors.
